Unauthorized API Access Due to Weak Authentication [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on API Gateway, Lambda Functions: Attackers could attempt to bypass API Gateway authentication by exploiting misconfigured IAM policies, intercepting/stealing API keys, or exploiting authentication vulnerabilities. An attacker obtains an API key through client-side code exposure or intercepts it in transit, then uses it to send unauthorized push notifications to all users.

Device Token Exfiltration from DynamoDB [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-359] on DynamoDB, Lambda Functions: Insufficient encryption of device tokens in DynamoDB or overly permissive IAM policies could allow unauthorized access to token data. An attacker exploits an overly permissive IAM role to access DynamoDB and extract device tokens, which are then used to send unauthorized notifications.

Insecure Direct Lambda Function Access [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on Lambda Functions, VPC: Lambda functions not properly configured within a VPC could be directly invoked if IAM policies are misconfigured. An attacker discovers Lambda function ARNs and exploits misconfigured IAM policies to directly invoke functions, bypassing API Gateway controls.

Sensitive Data Exposure in CloudWatch Logs [Information Disclosure, CWE-532] on CloudWatch, Lambda Functions, API Gateway: Insufficient log sanitization could lead to sensitive data being written to CloudWatch logs, which could then be accessed by unauthorized users with CloudWatch access. An attacker with CloudWatch access discovers sensitive information in logs, including device tokens and notification payloads.

Insecure Communication Channel with User Devices [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-319] on Pinpoint, SNS, User Devices: Without proper encryption and secure communication channels, push notifications could be intercepted or modified in transit. An attacker performs a man-in-the-middle attack to intercept or modify push notifications before they reach user devices.

Token Replay Attacks [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-294] on Lambda Functions, DynamoDB: Device tokens that aren't properly invalidated after use or don't have expiration times could be reused for unauthorized notifications. An attacker captures a valid device token and reuses it multiple times to send unauthorized notifications, even after the token should have been invalidated.

Analytics Data Pipeline Exposure [Information Disclosure, CWE-200] on Kinesis Firehose, S3, Analytics: Misconfigured S3 bucket permissions or Kinesis Firehose delivery settings could expose analytics data to unauthorized users. An attacker discovers an S3 bucket with insufficient access controls and extracts analytics data containing sensitive user information.
